entries.headline: GOAT Industries to acquire casino contract revenues from Epoxy AI
entries.dek: The deal, paid in 11,377,600 GOAT shares at C$0.25 each, covers rights to six U.S. tribal casino and sportsbook contracts.
entries.caption: An empty casino floor sits dark before opening, as a gaming operator restructures contract revenue through a share-based deal.

sources.title: GOAT Industries Signs Definitive Agreement To Acquire Epoxy AI Customer Contract Revenues

unverified_claims: Hank Frecon's statement that the agreement 'marks an important step forward in delivering on the strategy we outlined to shareholders' is a characterization by company management.
The description of a broader, previously announced acquisition strategy rests on the company's own characterization of its plans.
brief: GOAT Industries Ltd. (CSE: GOAT) said its subsidiary, Source Gaming Company, has signed a definitive agreement dated October 20 to acquire customer contract revenues from Epoxy AI, LLC. The consideration is 11,377,600 GOAT common shares at C$0.25 per share.

The agreement gives Source Gaming rights to revenues, receivables and other amounts owed under six Epoxy customer contracts with U.S. tribal casinos and other casino and sports book operators. Epoxy is to assign the underlying contracts within six months of closing, subject to customer consents; until then, it will hold the revenue in trust for Source Gaming.

Completion is subject to conditions including the release of security interests and acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange, and either party may terminate the agreement if it has not closed by November 30, 2026. The release said a US$100,000 non-interest-bearing promissory note dated January 2026 remains outstanding and will survive completion of the transaction.
body: GOAT Industries Ltd. (CSE: GOAT) said its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Source Gaming Company, operating as BetSource, has entered into a definitive contract revenue assignment agreement dated October 20, 2026, with Epoxy AI, LLC. Under the agreement, Source Gaming will acquire customer contract revenues from Epoxy in exchange for 11,377,600 common shares of GOAT, issued at a price of C$0.25 per share.

The rights being acquired cover revenues, receivables and other amounts payable under six customer contracts Epoxy holds with U.S. tribal casinos and other established casino and sports book operators. Rather than transferring the underlying contracts immediately, the agreement structures the deal as an assignment of the revenue stream from those contracts to Source Gaming.

Epoxy is to formally assign the underlying customer contracts to Source Gaming within six months of closing, subject to the consent of the customers involved. Until that assignment takes place, the release said Epoxy will continue to perform its obligations under the contracts and will hold the resulting revenue in trust for Source Gaming.

Completion of the transaction is subject to the satisfaction or waiver of certain conditions, including the release of applicable security interests, other necessary approvals, and acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange. Either party may terminate the agreement if the transaction has not closed by November 30, 2026. Separately, the release said a US$100,000 non-interest-bearing promissory note dated January 2026 remains outstanding between the companies and will survive completion of the transaction.

"This Agreement marks an important step forward in delivering on the strategy we outlined to shareholders," Hank Frecon, acting chief executive of Source Gaming Company, said in the release. The release described the transaction as advancing an acquisition strategy GOAT had previously outlined to shareholders in August 2026.

entries.headline: Howard Hughes Holdings set to join S&P SmallCap 600
entries.dek: The change follows CRH plc's acquisition of Arcosa Inc., which closed the same day, and takes effect before trading opens on October 28.
entries.caption: Morning light over a city skyline of office towers, as index providers rebalance ahead of the market open.

sources.title: Howard Hughes Holdings Set to Join S&P SmallCap 600

unverified_claims: S&P Dow Jones Indices' description of itself as 'the largest global resource for index-based concepts, data and research' is the index provider's own characterization.
brief: Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HHH) will replace Arcosa Inc. (NYSE: ACA) in the S&P SmallCap 600 effective before the opening of trading on October 28, S&P Dow Jones Indices said. The change follows the acquisition of Arcosa by S&P 500 constituent CRH plc (NYSE: CRH), in a deal that closed October 23.

S&P Dow Jones Indices, which manages benchmarks including the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, classifies Howard Hughes under the Real Estate sector and had classified Arcosa under Industrials. The index provider said it operates as a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI).

The release did not disclose the terms of CRH's acquisition of Arcosa beyond confirming that the deal had closed on October 23. The index addition and deletion take effect automatically on the stated date.
body: Howard Hughes Holdings Inc. (NYSE: HHH) will replace Arcosa Inc. (NYSE: ACA) in the S&P SmallCap 600, S&P Dow Jones Indices said, effective before the opening of trading on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. The index provider classified Howard Hughes under the Real Estate sector and had classified Arcosa under Industrials.
The change was triggered by S&P 500 constituent CRH plc's (NYSE: CRH) acquisition of Arcosa, in a deal that closed the same day the index change was announced, October 23.

S&P Dow Jones Indices describes itself as the largest global resource for index-based concepts, data and research, home to benchmarks including the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average, and said more assets are invested in products based on its indices than any other provider globally. It operates as a division of S&P Global (NYSE: SPGI).

Beyond confirming that the CRH-Arcosa transaction had closed, the release disclosed no further terms of that acquisition, and gave no reason beyond the acquisition itself for Arcosa's removal from the index.

entries.headline: Hyperliquid Strategies boosts buyback authorization to $100 million
entries.dek: The board extended the program's expiration from December 2026 to October 31, 2027, and said about $72 million remains available for buybacks under the enlarged authorization.
entries.caption: A trading floor glows before the open, as capital-return programs expand across digital-asset treasury companies.

sources.title: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc Announces Increase of Stock Repurchase Program to $100 Million

unverified_claims: The characterization that the increase 'reflects the Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy' is the company's own stated rationale.
The company's description of itself as a digital asset treasury company focused on HYPE token accumulation for U.S. and institutional investors is the company's own description.
brief: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (Nasdaq: PURR) said its board of directors increased the company's stock repurchase authorization to $100 million from $30 million, with about $72 million remaining available for buybacks. The board also extended the program's termination date to October 31, 2027, from December 5, 2026.

The company describes itself as a digital asset treasury company focused on accumulating HYPE, the native token of the Hyperliquid blockchain network, for U.S. and institutional investors. The release said repurchases may occur through open market transactions, privately negotiated transactions, or other means permitted under federal securities laws.

The timing, number and value of any shares repurchased will depend on the stock price, market conditions and legal requirements, and remain at management's discretion, the release said. The board may extend, suspend or discontinue the program at any time without notice.
body: Hyperliquid Strategies Inc. (Nasdaq: PURR) said its board of directors has authorized an increase to the company's stock repurchase program, raising the total authorization to $100 million from $30 million. The board also extended the program's termination date, pushing it out to October 31, 2027, from its original expiration of December 5, 2026. The company said approximately $72 million remains available for repurchases under the expanded authorization.

A share repurchase, or buyback, program authorizes a company to buy back its own outstanding stock up to a set dollar amount, rather than committing it to purchase any fixed number of shares by a set date. The release said Hyperliquid Strategies may carry out repurchases through open market transactions, privately negotiated transactions, or other methods permitted under federal securities laws, with the timing, volume and price of any purchases left to management's discretion.

The company describes itself as a digital asset treasury company built around HYPE, the native token of the Hyperliquid blockchain network, aiming to give U.S. and institutional investors capital-efficient exposure to the token through staking and yield strategies. The release said the increase "reflects the Board's confidence in the Company's long-term capital strategy and provides flexibility to buy back PURR shares as part of the Company's broader treasury management framework."

The company said the timing, number and value of any shares repurchased will depend on the stock price, market conditions and legal requirements, and will remain at management's discretion. It said the board may extend, suspend or discontinue the program at any time without notice, and that there is no guarantee as to how many shares will ultimately be bought back.
Beyond the dollar figures, the revised expiration date and the board's general statement of rationale, the release provides no additional detail on the buyback program.

entries.headline: Canadian retail sales rose 1.2% in August
entries.dek: Statistics Canada said sales reached $74.6 billion, with gains in all nine retail subsectors and a preliminary estimate pointing to a 0.7% rise in September.
entries.caption: Shoppers move through a plaza at dusk, as Statistics Canada reports another month of broad-based retail gains.
brief: Statistics Canada said Canadian retail sales rose 1.2% to $74.6 billion in August, with sales increasing across all nine retail subsectors. Motor vehicle and parts dealers led the gain, also up 1.2%, while gasoline stations rose 1.7% and food and beverage retailers increased 1.1%, their first gain in three months.

Core retail sales, which exclude gasoline stations and motor vehicle and parts dealers, rose 1.1%. In volume terms, which adjust for price changes, sales were also up 1.2%. E-commerce sales totalled $5.6 billion, an increase of 1.1%, representing 7.6% of total retail trade for the month, the agency said.

Ontario led provincial gains, up 2.2% to $28.5 billion, followed by British Columbia, up 2.1% to $10.0 billion. Sales declined in Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, New Brunswick, Alberta, Yukon and Nunavut, by 0.1% to 0.6%. A preliminary estimate for September points to a 0.7% increase, the agency said.
body: Statistics Canada said retail sales in Canada rose 1.2% to $74.6 billion in August 2026, with increases recorded across all nine retail subsectors tracked in the survey. Motor vehicle and parts dealers posted the largest gain, also up 1.2%; gasoline stations rose 1.7%; and food and beverage retailers increased 1.1%, their first gain in three months, the agency said.

Core retail sales, a measure that excludes gasoline stations and motor vehicle and parts dealers, rose 1.1% in August. In volume terms, which adjust the dollar figures for price changes, sales were also up 1.2%, indicating the increase reflected a rise in the quantity of goods sold rather than price alone.

Provincial results varied. Ontario led with a 2.2% increase to $28.5 billion in retail sales, and British Columbia followed with a 2.1% increase to $10.0 billion. Sales declined in six provinces and territories — Newfoundland and Labrador, Prince Edward Island, New Brunswick, Alberta, Yukon and Nunavut — by between 0.1% and 0.6%, the agency said. E-commerce sales totalled $5.6 billion in August, up 1.1% from July and accounting for 7.6% of total retail trade for the month.

Statistics Canada also published an advance estimate for September 2026, suggesting retail sales rose 0.7% for the month. The agency said the estimate is preliminary, based on a survey response rate of 58.5% compared with a historical average of 86.8%, and is subject to revision. The retail sales data are seasonally adjusted and reported in current dollars, the agency said.
